ai.description: *Boiga ceylonensis* reaches 1.2 meters. It features a brownish-grey body with dark, irregular crossbands and a distinct, triangular head. A dark streak runs from the eye to the jaw angle.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga ceylonensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-edged, pale vertebral spots and a characteristic dark "Y" or "V" shaped mark on the nape of its head.
ai.habitat: The Sri Lanka Cat Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically ranging from lowlands up to elevations of approximately 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sri Lanka Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal, often seen slithering through forest canopies or near human settlements in search of geckos and small birds to hunt.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Sri Lanka Cat Snake is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, often between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga ceylonensis* is endemic to Sri Lanka and the Western Ghats of India, typically inhabiting moist forests from lowlands up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
